seed: Objects of type `target` under action ACTION1 with touching neighbours [reflection,wall] show mixed outcomes: h,pixels x1, no_change x1. Find the condition in the before state that decides the outcome. Start from this kind of condition: the presence, type or relative position of a neighbouring object. Verify it against every transition before you keep it.

synth.notes:
Mechanics: frame parsed into 21x21 blocks: horizontal wall axis (ring 10) on block row A, pieces (ring 5), solid targets (11); selection is shown by 0 centres.
A5 cycles axis -> pieces by size desc -> axis; A1/A2 move the axis or piece up/down, A3/A4 move pieces left/right (no-op for the axis); pieces are blocked by bounds and other pieces.
Reflections: each piece block (c,r) with r!=A goes to (c,2A-r) as ring 4 with fill 4, clipped, skipped on piece blocks. Render stack piece>refl>target>wall; centre = first solid, else topmost fill.
Hypothesis resolved: the mixed target A1 outcome is the reflection ring covering/uncovering target cells as the axis moves, not a target field.
HUD: col 63 gets one 11->12 cell per state-changing action. Unconfirmed: whether blocked piece moves tick, plus win/reset. 29/29 with and without hidden state.
